assessment.nobel_worthiness: Can Xue has one of the most uncompromising and recognizable voices on the list. Her dreamlike, anti-realist fiction (Frontier; Love in the New Millennium, plus many earlier stories and novels) breaks with conventional psychology, space and causality. The formal radicalism is sustained over decades and is not a single-book effect. Her work is often read alongside Kafka and Borges, but the vision is her own. The case rests on distinctiveness, formal achievement and imaginative depth.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: a body of experimental fiction in Chinese that reimagines the narrative imagination and the boundaries between inner and outer worlds. One writer, one oeuvre, with no ambiguity of credit.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre has been built over several decades and is stylistically consistent while still developing. It is mature enough for a full-oeuvre judgment, and her international reception has been growing.
uncertainties: Only part of the oeuvre is in translation, and the quality of the translations cannot be independently verified here.
The prose is deliberately opaque, so a judgment of linguistic achievement depends on the translators.
The corpus is very large and my knowledge of it is uneven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cărtărescu has built an ambitious, visionary prose project of dense patterning in which memory, the body and metaphysics are fused (the Blinding trilogy; Solenoid). The scale and formal ambition are exceptional, and he also writes poetry and essays. The case rests on imaginative and intellectual depth and on a distinctive, immersive voice. The risk is excess and self-referentiality in the longest books.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: an encyclopedic, visionary prose oeuvre in Romanian that turns the interior life and the body into cosmology, with roots in poetry. A single writer with a clear and coherent contribution.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre is substantial and was developed over several decades from the 1980s onward. The major prose works are already established, so the timing is sound.
uncertainties: The extent and quality of the English and Swedish translations of the very long books are uncertain.
Judgments of the ornate Romanian prose depend heavily on translators.
The balance between ambition and control across the trilogy is hard to assess from public knowledge alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: NDiaye's fiction and plays have a precise and unsettling voice. Through narrators who are estranged, shifting or unreliable, they expose exclusion, family power and unstable belonging (Three Strong Women; My Heart Hemmed In; Rosie Carpe). The prose is economical, and the uncanny is anchored in social reality. The sustained quality across novels and plays is high.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: a French-language oeuvre of fiction and drama that makes the uncanny a means of examining social and familial power and belonging. Credit is clear.
assessment.maturity: She has published since her teens and has a large, consistent body of work. Her reputation is secure in French, and the timing is reasonable. The theatre is less known outside France.
uncertainties: The subtlety of her French style may be partly lost in translation.
The plays are less accessible internationally, and my knowledge of them is thinner.
It is uncertain whether the whole oeuvre has the scale and range of the strongest competitors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Zurita's work is distinctive in scale and conception. Large poetic sequences (Purgatory; Anteparadise) and landscape-scale and skywriting interventions turn the suffering of the Chilean dictatorship years into a collective, memorial form. The ambition extends beyond the page, and the poetry remains rooted in lyric and linguistic invention. The risk is that the public gestures may carry as much weight as the poems themselves.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: a Spanish-language poetic oeuvre that transforms political trauma into memorial and cosmic form. One writer, clearly credited. The citation should rest on the poems and not on political symbolism.
assessment.maturity: A long career from the late 1970s onward with consistent preoccupations and continuing production. The work is fully mature.
uncertainties: Poetry translates unevenly, and the typographic and visual aspects are hard to judge without the originals.
Political and historical significance must be kept separate from literary merit.
My knowledge of the later books is thinner than of the early sequences.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Michon writes dense, compressed prose with a markedly individual syntax and rhythm. In Small Lives and The Eleven he turns obscure lives and the history of art into narrative inquiry. The linguistic achievement is high and the voice is unmistakable. The oeuvre is small in volume but of great intensity.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: a French-language prose oeuvre that makes the fragments of obscure and artistic lives into concentrated literature. Credit is unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre was built over four decades and is stylistically consistent. The compact size is a deliberate feature, but it may limit breadth for a prize that honours a whole body of work.
uncertainties: The style is extremely hard to translate, so the English and Swedish versions may flatten the achievement.
The oeuvre is smaller than those of several other candidates.
The thematic range may be narrower than the strongest cases offer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright's large, polyphonic novels (Carpentaria; The Swan Book) reshape the form of the novel through Indigenous oral practice, sovereignty and ecological time. The ambition and the formal invention are real, and the imaginative scale is considerable. She is also a significant nonfiction writer.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: English-language fiction that remakes the novel through Aboriginal storytelling traditions and the long time of land and climate. Credit is clear. The citation should rest on formal and linguistic achievement, not on representation.
assessment.maturity: A strong body of work, but a smaller number of major novels than most others on the list. It is still developing, and a full-oeuvre judgment may come a little early.
uncertainties: The number of major works is limited relative to the other candidates.
Her later work is less familiar to me, so the sustained-quality judgment is less certain.
Extended novels with oral structures are hard to assess from public knowledge alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson's hybrid works (Autobiography of Red; Nox; Eros the Bittersweet) remake the boundaries between classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual form. The intelligence is exceptional and the voice is unmistakable. Formal invention is central to her output, and Nox is a distinctive work of mourning in book form.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: English-language poetry and hybrid writing that brings classical antiquity into radical contemporary forms. Credit is clear. Whether the genre-crossing counts as literary achievement within Nobel's will's framework is a question for the committee.
assessment.maturity: A long career with sustained quality, and she remains active. The oeuvre is mature, though much of it is slim in volume.
uncertainties: The classical and scholarly allusions require expert reading.
Her work depends heavily on the visual and material form of the book, which can be lost in translation.
Some of the work could be judged more as scholarship or experiment than as sustained literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adonis has remade Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and an extended dialogue with inherited forms (Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses). His influence on modern Arabic poetry is widely recognized, and the critical essays are an important part of the case. The concern is how much of the achievement is available outside Arabic.
assessment.attribution: Citation scope: Arabic-language poetry and criticism that renewed the tradition from within. Credit is clear. The citation should rest on the poetry and its formal achievement, not on his public role.
assessment.maturity: A very long career from the mid-twentieth century, and the work is fully mature. The timing question is the age of the writer, which is not a literary criterion.
uncertainties: Arabic poetry's formal achievement is only partly accessible in translation, and I cannot verify the translations.
I know the early and middle work better than the most recent.
Influence and reputation must be kept separate from literary quality.
